pr.title: Plan running the full gate once per head, in CI
pr.head: f770afdba5cda87763be63d01311a3b6996cee5e

summary: Projector's skills tell three parties to run a repository's full validation gate, its complete set of tests and checks, on every head of a pull request. The author or the fixer runs it before each push, CI runs it on the push, and the reviewer runs it again, through project review gate when review.gate is set in .projector.toml, or from the repository's instructions otherwise. Two of those three runs check code that was already checked.

This pull request adds only a plan, docs/projects/gate-in-ci/readme.md, at status: ready. The plan adds a review.gate_checks setting that names the GitHub Actions check runs that run a repository's suite. Where the setting is set:

• The author and the fixer run the tests that cover their change and the review.gate command before a push, not the full suite.
  • The reviewer runs project review gate, which waits up to 30 minutes for the named check runs on the head and writes their result into the same gate record a local run writes. So the incremental review's rule, which asks for a passing gate when the merge base moved, reads a CI result without change. The gate reads CI for an untrusted head too, because reading a result runs none of the head's code, but it runs the review.gate command only on a trusted head.
  • The watch daemon sends a new CHECKS event to the fixer when a check or status on the head fails, leaving out Projector's own projector/review status. It reads the rollup's counts by state and reads later pages of contexts only when those counts show a failure that the first 20 contexts lack.

A head that changed a file behind a named check, such as its workflow file or a local action that workflow uses, decided what its own check ran. So gate refuses to use CI for that head. A repository without the setting keeps today's behavior. The code, skills, and docs follow in a later pull request.

cards.title: What the gate's exit codes mean
cards.html:
ExitWhenWhat the reviewer does
0The review.gate command, if it ran, passed and every named check concluded successCounts the gate as passed
1The command failed, or a named check concluded failure or timed_outTreats it as a failing gate
75CI gave no evidence: no completed run within 30 minutes, no run coming, or a check that was cancelled, skipped, or waits for approvalRuns the full gate locally on a trusted head, and reviews by reading on an untrusted one

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• The first review, of 16f042b, opened four findings: a false CHECKS event from projector/review, a missing check that signed off untested, a local action that escaped the workflow refusal, and a check-runs read limited to one page. All four were fixed at 9aa0747.
  • The review of 9aa0747 found that CHECKS read only the first 20 rollup contexts. That was fixed at f770afd, along with two suggestions about run statuses and conclusions.
  • The review of f770afd is clean, with one suggestion: leave a failed projector/review out of the counts before deciding to read another page.

groups.title: The plan for running the gate in CI
groups.kicker: The problem, the new setting, the gate's CI wait, the files behind a check, and the CHECKS event
intro: The plan is the whole change. § 2.1 walks through the flow after the change, step by step. § 2.2 defines the review.gate_checks setting, the two fields the gate record gains (checks and source), and the CHECKS event line. § 2.3 lists the change to each file. § 2.4 says how gate finds the files that decided what a check ran.

A check run is GitHub's record of one CI job on a commit. A commit status is a simpler state that any account with write access can post, which is how Projector posts its own projector/review sign-off. The rollup is GitHub's view of both kinds on a commit: an overall state and a paged list of contexts, one per check run or status. The gate counts only check runs from the github-actions app, so a commit status never counts as test evidence. The watch event reads the rollup's failed contexts.

checks.text: A plan at ready claims it is executable, so every question that blocks implementation must be answered or deferred. Its two open questions, a configurable wait and merge-queue checks, are deferred in § 6, and § 5 defers measuring the watch query's cost to the implementation.

files.note: The new plan: why the gate runs three times today, how the CI gate works for trusted and untrusted heads, and how each skill changes.

checks.text: An untrusted head's passing CI record cannot allow an incremental review: incremental_rules in src/projector/review.py refuses an untrusted head before it reads gate_passed. Checked in the code at the base.

The page read in § 2.1 step 7 ends when hasNextPage is false, and runs only when the counts show a failure the first page lacks. A GraphQL query on this pull request confirmed that the rollup's contexts connection has checkRunCountsByState, statusContextCountsByState, and pageInfo.
